request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (30,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 36.8% (95% band 33.3% to 40.9%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= -1: -0.3; 0: -0.5; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.55, 95% band [+2.43, +2.72]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 21.6% (95% band 19.5% to 24.8%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 74999: +0.5; 75000-154999: +0.09; 155000-464999: -0.3629; >= 465000: -1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.29, 95% band [-1.52, -1.06]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 9.2% (95% band 6.7% to 12.0%); rank 3 to 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1100: +0.2; >= 1101: -0.06 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.60, 95% band [-0.75, -0.39]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 8.8% (95% band 4.7% to 10.9%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 25368: -0.14; >= 25369: +0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.70, 95% band [+0.31, +0.94]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 7.0% (95% band 4.2% to 8.3%); rank 4 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2131: +0.037; >= 2132: -0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.21, 95% band [-0.31, -0.05]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 3.5% (95% band 1.5% to 5.1%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.07, 95% band [-0.09, +0.21]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 3.0% (95% band 1.1% to 6.2%); rank 5 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.33 (95% band [+0.07, +0.62]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 195,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.1% to 2.9%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.10 (95% band [+0.00, +0.17]) from x = 1 (5th percentile) to x = 3 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.4% (95% band 0.4% to 2.7%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.02, 95% band [-0.08, +0.14]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 3.3% (95% band 1.7% to 3.7%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.98 (95% band +0.55 to +1.17) when `AGE` = 23, +0.31 (95% band -0.08 to +0.62) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.37 (95% band +0.11 to +0.57) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.31 (95% band -0.44 to -0.04) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `AGE & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.8% (95% band 1.2% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.14 (95% band -0.05 to +0.34) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.09 (95% band -0.29 to +0.17) when `BILL_AMT2` = 195,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 195,000: +0.39 (95% band +0.13 to +0.77) when `AGE` = 23, +0.16 (95% band -0.10 to +0.47) when `AGE` = 53.
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.47 (95% band +2.34 to +2.66) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +2.78 (95% band +2.47 to +2.88) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.02 (95% band -0.10 to +0.13) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.33 (95% band +0.00 to +0.40) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT2 & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.2%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 19,000: -0.23 (95% band -0.32 to -0.02) when `AGE` = 23, -0.16 (95% band -0.38 to -0.01) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: -0.05 (95% band -0.16 to +0.22) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.01 (95% band -0.17 to +0.21) when `PAY_AMT2` = 19,000.
- `PAY_0 & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.59 (95% band +2.43 to +2.77) when `AGE` = 23, +2.53 (95% band +2.42 to +2.69) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.19 (95% band -0.05 to +0.30) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.13 (95% band -0.08 to +0.25) when `PAY_0` = 2.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The most important driver of predicted default is the repayment status in the latest month, September 2005: applicants who were one or more months behind on payments carry much higher predicted risk, with the effect rising sharply once delays reach two months or more, while applicants who paid in full or revolved credit carry lower risk."},{"id":2,"text":"The second most important driver is the size of the applicant's credit limit: lower limits are associated with higher predicted default risk, and very high limits (465,000 NT dollars and above) are associated with lower risk."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month and the latest bill amount each matter somewhat less; a payment of 1,101 NT dollars or more lowers predicted risk slightly, and larger bills raise it slightly, with wide uncertainty on the size of the bill effect."},{"id":4,"text":"The amount paid in the previous month also lowers predicted risk when it is above about 2,131 NT dollars, but this effect is modest."},{"id":5,"text":"Age has an overall effect the data do not settle, but it interacts with the latest bill amount: a larger bill raises risk more for younger applicants (around 23) than for older ones (around 53), and the effect of age itself depends on the size of the bill."},{"id":6,"text":"Education and the amount paid two months earlier have small importance, and the data do not clearly establish a consistent direction or shape for their effects."},{"id":7,"text":"Several interactions are real but minor; the strongest is between repayment status and education, where the education effect is small when the applicant is not delinquent and only somewhat larger when delinquent, so the overall picture rests mainly on repayment status and credit limit."}]}
